info.name: Leave Request Module
info.description:
Leave requests with TWO-STAGE APPROVAL.

A regular employee's request goes to the HEAD OF DEPARTMENT first, then to the ADMIN.
The head of department's own request — and any request from an employee with no department, or whose department has no head — goes straight to the ADMIN.

`status` keeps its old meaning: it stays `pending` for the whole journey and only becomes `approved` when the admin signs off (payroll reads `status`, so nothing there changes).
`approval_stage` says who must act next:
  - `hod`       → waiting for the head of department
  - `admin`     → waiting for the admin (HOD leg done or not needed)
  - `completed` → approved / rejected / cancelled

`hod_status`: `not_required` | `pending` | `approved` | `rejected`.
A HOD rejection ends the request immediately — status becomes `rejected` and the admin never sees it.

request.description:
Submit a leave request. The backend decides the approval route automatically from the employee's department and its head — the client sends nothing extra.

The response carries `approval_route` so the UI can say who is reviewing it: `approval_stage` (`hod` or `admin`), the HOD's employee id, and `skip_reason` when the HOD leg was skipped (`employee_is_head_of_department`, `department_has_no_head`, `employee_has_no_department`).

item.name: Head of Department — Stage 1 Approval
item.description: Authorised by identity, not role: the caller's employee record must be the `head_employee_id` of a department. A HOD normally holds the Employee role, so a plain employee token is expected here. Non-HOD callers get 403.

request.description: Requests from the caller's department waiting on them. `stage` accepts `hod` (default — my action queue), `admin` (already forwarded, waiting on the admin), or `all`. Optional `status` filter. `pending_count` drives the inbox badge.
